title: POC weekly: access & environment quirks review
summary: Weekly checkpoint covering staging access gaps, unexpected env behaviors (KV cache misses, transient 502s), quantization profile tuning, and privacy/KMS handoff. Agreed on running a targeted bench with 512/1024 token distribution and to share security pack + SSO steps.
topics: next benchmark run and success criteria
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-23 15:00 PST | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Ava, Marcus, Jordan / Sofia, Tom, Priya, Ethan

[00:00] Ava Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. We have 40 minutes. Quick check, did anyone get the staging creds earlier this morning?
[00:08] Tom Blake: I did, thanks. I was able to curl the gateway but noticed a bunch of cache misses initially, like almost every request for the first 10 minutes.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Yeah that matches what we saw on the probe — KV cache warmup was slow because the prefix distribution is different from your prod traces. We pushed a warmup script, but looks like your traffic shape has a lot more unique prefixes.
[00:33] Sofia Ramirez: Right, our user journeys have long tails, lots of unique prompts. Is that something Redwood can mitigate without increasing latency too much?
[00:42] Marcus Lee: There's a tradeoff: more aggressive prefix caching reduces token cost but can increase memory pressure. We suggested a tiered approach — short-term warmup and then adaptive eviction. Also we can change the batching window slightly.
[00:55] Priya Singh: Quick privacy note — before we run any warmup scripts, we need confirmation on data retention and KMS usage, Priya here.
[01:05] Ava Chen: Absolutely, Priya. We'll send the security pack after this call — includes SOC two certs, KMS integration notes, and where logs are retained. Note: our private deployments use customer-managed KMS, and for hosted we do envelope encryption, but we'll detail both.
[01:22] Ethan Zhou: I also hit an intermittent 502 on longer sequences, around 750 tokens. Not sure if it's timeout or memory.
[01:31] Marcus Lee: We saw that on the trace — the runtime evicted keys during generation on some runs, leading to a retried request and a 502 surface. We're going to test increasing KV cache allocation for the model variant you're using (the 13B q4 variant).
[01:46] Sofia Ramirez: Model variant... we were originally on the 13B q8, but switched to q4 earlier to save cost. I might have that backwards — sorry, lots of names.
[01:55] Ava Chen: No worries, these names are messy — sometimes Fireflies even writes Redwud instead of Redwood.
[02:03] Tom Blake: Ha. On costs — Priya is worried about predictable spend for Q1. If we push more memory to cache, does that spike our monthly?
[02:12] Marcus Lee: Slightly. But we can do a canary: allocate more cache for 10% of traffic and measure hit-rate uplift and cost delta. If hit rate improves significantly, unit cost per token drops.
[02:28] Jordan Park: Also there's quantization options: 8-bit (8-bit quant) vs more aggressive 4-bit. With 4-bit sometimes you see a perf hit for certain prompts — hallucinations or degens — so we recommended running eval prompt sets.
[02:44] Ethan Zhou: We have an eval suite — will share the prompting set. Can Redwood run the eval and compare generations across q8 vs q4?
[02:52] Marcus Lee: Yes, we can. We usually run the eval in a dedicated bench cluster to avoid affecting your staging pool. We'll include per-token latency, p95, and divergence metrics.
[03:05] Sofia Ramirez: Great. On the access side, one snag: SSO SAML wasn't fully configuring; our identity team reports the AssertionConsumerURL is mismatched.
[03:14] Ava Chen: We'll re-send the SSO steps. Jordan, can you follow up with their IdP team after?
[03:18] Jordan Park: Yep. I'll open a ticket and loop in the SSO engineer.
[03:22] Priya Singh: Also need to confirm audit logs retention window, and whether logs include prompt text or only metadata.
[03:29] Ava Chen: For hosted, logs redact prompt text by default, retained 30 days unless you buy extended retention. For private, you control retention and can opt in or out of storing raw text. We'll add that to the security pack.
[03:43] Tom Blake: Back to the 502s — what's the immediate mitigation?
[03:46] Marcus Lee: Short term: increase request timeout and retry logic in the gateway, and do a focused bench with increased KV allotment. Replace aggressive eviction policy with LRU tuning. That should cut the transient errors.
[04:02] Ethan Zhou: What's the timeline for the bench run and results?
[04:05] Ava Chen: We can kick it off tomorrow if you provide the eval prompts and token distribution -- aim for results in 48 hours.
[04:12] Sofia Ramirez: 48 hours is fine. We need to see p95 under 350ms for 128 token workloads to qualify as success for our QA.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: Noted — p95 <350ms target for 128 tokens. We'll also capture cost-per-1000 tokens and hit-rate.
[04:28] Priya Singh: One more compliance question — we may need an on-prem option for a small subset of PHI workloads. How feasible is Redwood Private for a small VPC block?
[04:36] Ava Chen: Redwood Private is doable; we offer a small-footprint on-prem package but it needs a minimum commit for support. We'll include the private deployment datasheet and estimate in the docs pack.
[04:47] Sofia Ramirez: Budgeting conversation aside, can you summarize the plan for the bench and immediate actions?
[04:53] Ava Chen: Sure. 1) Redwood to run bench comparing q8 vs q4 with your eval prompts (start tomorrow), 2) Increase KV cache on canary traffic to measure hit-rate, 3) Temp gateway retry/timeout tweak, 4) Send security/KMS docs and SSO steps, 5) Jordan to open SSO ticket.
[05:12] Tom Blake: Sounds good. Also, we'll provide the token distribution CSV and the eval set by EOD.
[05:19] Marcus Lee: Great. Any competitors mentioned by the team?
[05:23] Sofia Ramirez: We did some early work with Anthropic at proof-of-concept and a short bench in Vertex AI, but cost there was higher and throughput lower for our seq lengths.
[05:33] Ava Chen: Ok noted.
[05:35] Priya Singh: Quick clarification on KMS: do you support HSM-backed keys?
[05:39] Ava Chen: Yes — for private and dedicated we can integrate with customer HSM or cloud KMS-backed HSM; we'll detail in the pack and include expected audit artifacts.
[05:50] Ethan Zhou: Any gotchas we should be aware of during bench? Like sequence length distribution skew causing higher GC?
[05:58] Marcus Lee: The main gotcha is the KV cache thrash with a lot of unique prompts. Also, long sequences consume more transient memory. We'll instrument memory/eviction rates in the bench.
[06:10] Sofia Ramirez: Ok we're aligned. Can we do a follow-up mid-bench to look at initial telemetry?
[06:15] Ava Chen: Yes, we'll schedule a 20-minute mid-bench sync in 24 hours.
[06:20] Jordan Park: I'll propose a time.
[06:24] Priya Singh: Thanks, everyone.
[06:26] Ava Chen: Thanks all — recap in the notes and action items.

Note: transcription contains a few mis-hearings — e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" for Dedicated, "KV cash" variant in some auto-segments, and "SOC two" for SOC 2.
